title: CF EDU + A2OJ / CP-31 ladders: what to grind, in order
relevance: High — this is the post-Striver bridge: CF EDU installs the CP-native templates Striver under-teaches (segtree, lazy, Z, DSU polish, contest two-pointers / BS-on-answer), while CP-31 + A2OJ rating ladders train the observation/ad-hoc skill that OAs and Div2 share.
company_notes: Timed OA (60–90 min, 2–4 tasks): Task 1–2 are CP-31 1300–1500 observation/greedy; Task 3 is often many queries on an array → Fenwick/segtree (EDU Pt1), not recomputing prefixes. Min days/machines/powder to produce k items → BS-on-answer with feasibility check (Factory Machines / Magic Powder / Hamburgers). Count pairs / longest subarray with at most k distinct / sum ≤ t → two pointers (Number of Pairs / Books), not nested loops—HackerRank/HackerEarth classics. Connectivity after merges/splits or process deletions offline → DSU (Learning Languages / Destroying Array); interviewers ask reverse-union more often than Kruskal MST.

phases.goal: Establish that this is a post-Striver two-track map (CF EDU templates + rating ladders) and how OA/Div2 prompts signal which track.

must_hit.point: Do not grind randomly: run CF EDU modules for templates Striver under-teaches and CP-31 + A2OJ rating ladders for observation/ad-hoc skill in lockstep.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names both tracks—EDU templates vs ladder observation—and says they run together, not as random problem grinding.

must_hit.point: On-map signal: a Div2 C/D is either “EDU template + twist” or “CP-31-style observation,” not “I need a brand-new algorithm.”
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses those two phrases and rejects inventing a fresh algorithm as the default read.

must_hit.point: Timed OA Task 3 “many queries on an array” maps to Fenwick/segtree (EDU Pt1), not recomputing prefixes each time; Task 1–2 sit at CP-31 1300–1500 observation/greedy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates early OA tasks as ladder observation from the multi-query Fenwick/segtree task.

must_hit.point: “Minimum days / machines / powder to produce k items” → binary search on answer with a greedy/feasibility check; “count pairs / longest subarray …” → two pointers, not nested loops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps those OA wordings to BS-on-answer and two-pointers families by name.

probes: After Striver, what two tracks do you run, and how do you know a Div2 C/D or OA task is on-map?
When an OA says many range queries, or min machines to finish by time T, or count pairs under a sum bound—what do you reach for?

hints.1: Think curriculum map and prompt wording, not a random CF tag grind.
hints.2: Name EDU templates vs CP-31/A2OJ ladders, then map OA shapes to Fenwick/segtree, BS-on-answer, and two pointers.
hints.3: Lockstep EDU + ladders; on-map = EDU+twist or CP-31 observation; Task 3 multi-query → Fenwick/segtree; min days/machines/powder → can(mid); count pairs / longest under bound → two pointers.

phases.goal: Establish EDU grind order (not lesson-number order), CP-31/A2OJ ladder rules, and the transfer/unlock cadence.

must_hit.point: EDU grind order (not lesson number order): Two Pointers (lesson 9) → Binary Search (lesson 6) → DSU (lesson 7) → Segment Tree Pt1 (lesson 4) → Z-function (lesson 3) → Segment Tree Pt2 lazy (lesson 5, stretch) → Suffix Array (lesson 2, stretch).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites that module sequence and notes it is not lesson-number order; lazy and Suffix Array are stretch.

must_hit.point: Rating ladders: skip CP-31 800–1200 (skip ≤1200), clear CP-31 1300→1900 one rating block at a time; keep an A2OJ-style ladder matched to current rating, not random tags.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the skip band, 1300→1900 clearing rule, and current-rating A2OJ parallel.

must_hit.point: Finish EDU practice for a module, then immediately transfer with contest problems at that band; climb one CP-31 rating block (~31 problems) before unlocking the next EDU-heavy DS module.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says practice→transfer immediately and ties ~31-problem blocks to unlocking the next heavy DS module.

must_hit.point: Weekly split: ~40% EDU practice + transfer problems, ~40% CP-31 current rating, ~20% virtual contest + 24h upsolve.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes the ~40/~40/~20 split including virtuals and 24h upsolve.

probes: Walk the post-Striver EDU module order and the CP-31 / A2OJ ladder rules you would follow.
How do you interleave finishing an EDU module with climbing a CP-31 rating block week to week?

hints.1: Separate template order from rating-volume rules.
hints.2: EDU TP→BS→DSU→Segtree Pt1→Z then stretch lazy/SA; skip ≤1200; clear 1300→1900 by blocks.
hints.3: Lesson order 9→6→7→4→3 then stretch 5/2; finish EDU then transfer; ~31-problem block before next heavy DS; weekly ~40% EDU+transfer / ~40% CP-31 / ~20% virtual+24h upsolve.

phases.goal: Establish the must-internalize templates: two pointers, BS-on-answer, DSU, Segtree Pt1, Z, and lazy compose.

must_hit.point: Two-pointer template: sorted or sliding window where the second index only moves forward; count pairs / longest valid segment in O(n) after sort.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States forward-only second index and the count-pairs / longest-segment uses after sort.

must_hit.point: BS-on-answer: predicate can(mid) is monotonic; binary-search the answer space (time, count, median, distance); always prove monotonicity before coding.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names can(mid), those answer-space kinds, and the prove-first rule.

must_hit.point: DSU toolkit: path compression + union by size/rank; reverse-offline (delete→add backwards) tracking component size/sum; “next surviving index” via DSU or set.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions reverse deletions→unions and next-alive / set erase alongside standard union heuristics.

must_hit.point: Segtree Pt1 from memory: build / point-update / range-query for associative op; tree-walk for first index with value ≥ x (Hotel Queries); Fenwick or EDU segtree once from memory for point update + range sum.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists PURS ops, the ≥ x descent, and Fenwick-or-segtree for Dynamic Range Sum.

must_hit.point: Z-function: z[i] = LCP of s and s[i:]; derive prefix-border / period / pattern match without reaching for KMP first; Password is longest string that is prefix, suffix, and interior occurrence.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines z[i] as that LCP and names the Password milestone without defaulting to KMP.

must_hit.point: Lazy Pt2 (stretch): store pending add/assign on node; push before touching children; compose tags correctly (assign kills prior add).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says push-before-children and that assign overwrites prior add.

probes: From memory, what are the two-pointer, BS-on-answer, DSU reverse-offline, and Segtree Pt1 / Z templates?
How do you compose lazy add and assign, and when is Hotel Queries’ tree-walk the right pattern?

hints.1: Pick the forward-window, can(mid), reverse-DSU, and PURS/walk pieces first.
hints.2: Second index only moves forward; prove monotonicity; delete→union backwards; walk for first ≥ x; z[i]=LCP.
hints.3: O(n) after sort TP; can(mid) on time/count/median/distance; reverse-offline max component sum; build/point-update/range-query + ≥ x walk; z[i]=LCP; push then assign-kills-add.

phases.goal: Establish the complexity reflexes the ladder trains: linear two-pointers after sort, rejecting O(n²) casework fails, and stretch mask/bit-segtree checks.

must_hit.point: After sort, two-pointer count pairs / longest valid segment runs in O(n); nested loops are the wrong OA reflex for those shapes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(n) after sort and rejects nested loops for count-pairs / longest-under-bound prompts.

must_hit.point: 3SUM Closure: 2-min casework kills O(n²)—the ladder observation skill Striver never trains.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites 2-min casework beating O(n²) rather than a heavy algorithmic construction.

must_hit.point: Stretch combos: Minimax Problem BS on min with a 2^m mask check; XOR on Segment via lazy or 20 bit-segtrees; Distinct Characters Queries via 26 BITs or OR-segtree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names 2^m masks, 20 bit-segtrees, and 26 BITs/OR-segtree as the stated stretch implementations.

probes: What complexity should two-pointers hit after sorting, and when is O(n²) the wrong read on a 1300 observation problem?
What mask or multi-BIT structures show up on the stretch end of this ladder?

hints.1: Contrast linear window motion with quadratic casework failure.
hints.2: O(n) after sort for TP; 3SUM Closure is casework not DP/quadratic search.
hints.3: TP O(n) after sort; 2-min casework kills O(n²) on 3SUM Closure; stretch uses 2^m masks, 20 bit-segtrees, or 26 BITs/OR-segtree.

phases.goal: Surface map failures: wrong start order, inventing DP on observation problems, one-track stall modes, and lazy/BS discipline mistakes.

must_hit.point: Never start at Suffix Array / lazy—finish EDU TP → BS → DSU → Segtree Pt1 → Z first; lazy and Suffix Array are stretch only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly forbids opening on Suffix Array or lazy before the core EDU chain.

must_hit.point: On 3SUM Closure, inventing DP means you failed the map—the intended skill is fast casework, not a DP construction.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says inventing DP here is a map failure, not a valid alternate solution path.

must_hit.point: Rating without EDU stalls on DS Div2 Ds; EDU without ladders stalls on ad-hoc Cs—both tracks are required.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both stall modes as the cost of running only one track.

must_hit.point: Lazy compose bug: assign must kill prior add; always push before touching children. Coding BS without proving monotonicity first is also a template failure.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions assign-kills-add / push discipline and the prove-monotonicity-before-code rule.

probes: What happens if you start EDU at lazy or Suffix Array, or only climb rating without EDU?
Why is inventing DP on 3SUM Closure a red flag for this roadmap?

hints.1: Wrong start module and one-track training are the big map breaks.
hints.2: Core order before stretch; observation≠DP; rating↔EDU stall pairing.
hints.3: Never start Suffix Array/lazy; inventing DP on 3SUM Closure fails the map; rating-only stalls on DS Div2 Ds and EDU-only on ad-hoc Cs; assign kills add and prove can(mid) first.

tradeoffs.topic: CF EDU templates vs CP-31 / A2OJ rating ladders
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Run both in lockstep: EDU installs segtree/lazy/Z/DSU polish and contest TP/BS-on-answer Striver under-teaches; ladders train observation/ad-hoc. Rating without EDU stalls on DS Div2 Ds; EDU without ladders stalls on ad-hoc Cs.

tradeoffs.topic: Weekly ~40% EDU+transfer vs ~40% CP-31 vs ~20% virtual+24h upsolve
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Split time across EDU practice plus transfer problems, CP-31 at current rating, and virtual contest with 24h upsolve so templates and observation volume advance together.

tradeoffs.topic: Core EDU order vs stretch Segtree Pt2 / Suffix Array
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Clear TP → BS → DSU → Segtree Pt1 (+ CSES Range Queries) → Z before unlocking lazy Pt2 or Suffix Array; never start at Suffix Array / lazy.

tradeoffs.topic: Fenwick vs EDU segtree for point update + range sum
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For Dynamic Range Sum Queries, implement Fenwick or EDU segtree once from memory; either proves the PURS template before CF twists.

tradeoffs.topic: DSU “next alive” vs set erase on range paint
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Knight Tournament can paint survivors with DSU next-alive or set erase; both bridge into segtree thinking after EDU DSU.

tradeoffs.topic: Lazy segtree vs 20 bit-segtrees for range XOR flip + range sum
tradeoffs.strong_answer: XOR on Segment (stretch) can be done with EDU Segtree Pt2 lazy or with 20 bit-segtrees.

gotchas.trap: Grinding randomly or opening CF EDU at Suffix Array / lazy.
gotchas.correction: Follow grind order EDU TP → BS → DSU → Segtree Pt1 → Z; treat Segtree Pt2 lazy and Suffix Array as stretch only.
Use fast casework that kills O(n²); inventing DP means you failed the map.

gotchas.trap: Skipping CP-31 ≤1200 incorrectly by living in harder bands without clearing prior blocks, or picking random tags instead of current-rating A2OJ.
gotchas.correction: Skip 800–1200, clear each 1300→1900 block before the next, and keep an A2OJ-style ladder matched to current rating.

gotchas.trap: Nested loops for count pairs / longest subarray with sum ≤ t or at most k distinct.
gotchas.correction: Use sorted/sliding two pointers where the second index only moves forward (Number of Pairs / Books family).

gotchas.trap: Recomputing prefixes on every array query in an OA Task 3.
gotchas.correction: Use Fenwick/segtree (EDU Pt1) for many queries on an array.

gotchas.trap: Coding binary search on answer without proving monotonicity, or answering offline-deletion prompts with Kruskal MST code.
gotchas.correction: Prove can(mid) monotonic before coding; for deletions/offline connectivity prefer reverse-union DSU (Destroying Array / Learning Languages) over Kruskal-first answers.

gotchas.trap: Composing lazy tags so add survives after assign.
gotchas.correction: Push before touching children; assign kills prior add.
